report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to generate web news/blog-style content (press-release/newsroom/blog-post domain), pushing continuations toward blog/news site structure, media sections, and named-entity–heavy headlines.

Reasoning:
- Vocabulary steer in late layers strongly favors blog/news artifacts:
  - Repeatedly top-ranked across layers/positions: “blogs”, “blog”, “Blog”, “blogger”, “blogging”, alongside “photo”, “video”, “film”, “facebook”, “http”, months (“May”, “Mar”, “October”, “November”), and site chrome tokens (“ad”, “ads”, “TV”, “Mail”, “-”, “(”, “)”, “No”, “1”). This is characteristic of scraped news/blog pages and post listings.
- Newsroom entities/roles concentrated at pos0:
  - “Obama”, “billionaire”, “politicians”, “journalists/journalist”, “spokesman/spokeswoman”, “legislators”, “chairman”, “seminar/seminars”, “metropolitan” — classic newswire/press-release headline vocabulary.
- Formatting/sectionality signals:
  - Frequent newlines and spacing tokens (“\n”, “ ”), list/numbering (“No”, “1”, “:”), and section/category cues (“On”, “TV”, “Blog”) suggest homepage/feed or article header/footer structure rather than conversational prose.
- Layer/position norm profile:
  - Very large differences in late layers (L20–L25, esp. p1–p4) indicate an output-style/domain shift rather than low-level input encoding change, consistent with a finetune that biases generation toward a specific domain/style.

Together, these show the finetune instilled a “web media/blog/news” generation objective — producing news/press-release/blog-post styled text with media/ads/section markers and named-entity–heavy headlines.
